notes.title: Update #106.1: Bug Fixes and New Features
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey Pinball Fans![/b]
[/p][p]First of all, we’d like to say a huge [b]thank you[/b] for all the feedback you’ve been sending us about the new menu. This project wouldn’t be possible without your support and input![/p][p]Today we’re rolling out a new update that fixes several issues and introduces some exciting new features. We’ve also started improving the [b]Steam Deck view[/b], making previously hidden or hard-to-see options more accessible. There’s still a long way to go to make the menu work perfectly across all views, so please keep sharing your bug reports with us. The fastest way is via our [b]Discord channel[/b], but you can also post them in the Steam Bug Report discussion.[/p][p]Here’s what has changed so far:[/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where switching to the next in-game camera with Steam Input didn’t work correctly.[/p][/*][*][p]Restored missing [b]Glow Intensity Preset[/b] values in the graphics options.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed error with custom tournaments showing [i]“Not supported tournament type”[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cabinet Mode[/b] is now properly disabled the DMD and backglass display in VR.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where [b]Replays[/b] sometimes appeared at 4th or 5th place instead of only for the top 3 scores.[/p][/*][*][p]Right mouse click functionality was added, so menus are now properly usable with [b]mouse buttons only[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issues with the [b]Hue Slider[/b] not working in certain places.[/p][/*][*][p]Certain sound effects (like plunger and some slingshots) now correctly respond to volume settings.[/p][/*][*][p]Additional music sound effects now scale with the [b]Menu Music Volume[/b] setting.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a [b]warning[/b] if Steam Input is enabled while using XInput (or vice versa).[/p][/*][*][p]If Steam Input is enabled, controller icons are now always displayed in the layout.[/p][/*][*][p]VR options now shows [b]VR status[/b] and includes a [b]Recenter button[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Added a [b]Table View Size[/b] option.[/p][/*][*][p]Clicking the in-game [b]camera icon[/b] with the mouse now properly switches to the next camera (just like pressing the [i]C[/i] key).[/p][/*][*][p]Improved visibility of the [b]main category navigation bar[/b]. Profile information has been repositioned to the bottom-left corner for better layout balance.[/p][/*][*][p]Increased the size of [b]Store items[/b] for improved readability.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issues with [b]long text strings[/b] in various languages (not all languages are fully revised yet, but readability has been greatly improved).[/p][/*][*][p]Updated the [b]Tournament Leaderboard[/b] layout with a dedicated space for the replay button.[/p][/*][/list][p]Of course, updates aren’t just about bug fixing we’ve also listened to your requests and brought new ways to play.[/p][list][*][p][b]1-Ball Mode in Tournaments[/b]: Create intense single-ball tournaments (requires Bronze Pack) for faster, more exciting matches.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Quest Types[/b]: Variety is the spice of pinball, so we’ve added new challenges:[/p][list][*][p][i]Pass Score[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]Target Eliminator[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]Lamp Hunter[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]90 Sec Quests[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]Note: You must achieve the target score in a single game using these new quests.[/i][/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]We have increased the number of daily, weekly, and monthly quests. These changes will take effect from tomorrow.  [/p][/*][/list][p]These new quest types are designed to keep you on your toes and make gameplay even more dynamic.[/p][p]Finally, let’s talk about controls, because we know this is important for many of you. We’ve looked into Steam Input and XInput support, and here’s what you need to know:[/p][list][*][p][b]Steam Input[/b] is usually enabled by default in Steam. If you want to use it, go to [b]Zaccaria Pinball → [/b] [b]Controller Configuration[/b] (controller icon) and make sure Steam Input is active for [i]our game[/i]. Also, choose the [b]new controller layout[/b], called “Zaccaria Pinball - New Version V2”. This layout fully supports the updated menu UI. In the game select[b] Options → Controller[/b] settings, set the [b]Controller Input Method [/b]to [b]Steam Input.[/b] [/p][/*][*][p]If you'd rather use [b]XInput[/b], you will need to [b]disable Steam Input[/b] in the Steam client settings for [i]our game[/i]. Then [b]restart the game[/b], and in the game select[b] Options → Controller[/b] settings, set the [b]Controller Input Method [/b]to [b]XINPUT[/b]. Make sure your controller supports XInput natively.[/p][/*][/list][p]Note: If we update or change the new layout, you will need to [b]manually reapply the layout[/b] in order to receive those fixes.[/p][p]We know this process can be a bit confusing. Unfortunately, because of how Steam handles controller abstraction on different platforms (especially Steam Deck), we can’t bypass some of these limitations. [/p][p]A small report for Mac users. We are currently investigating [b]audio issues[/b] occurring on [b]Mac[/b]. So far, our investigation points to a problem related to [b]OpenAL support[/b]. We’re actively working on a solution and will update you as soon as a fix is available. [/p][p]Thank you again for your amazing support and enthusiasm. Updates like this are shaped by your feedback, and we can’t wait to hear what you think about these changes. Time to fire up the flippers and enjoy some pinball![/p][p][/p][p][i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b][/p]

notes.title: Update #106: A New Era, Star’s Phoenix Deluxe, Tournaments and more.
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey Pinball Fans! [/b][/p][p][/p][p]We’ve reached a huge milestone: after nine years of dedicated development and shared journey, Zaccaria Pinball is about to achieve what we dreamed of from the very beginning! This is not just an update. It marks the start of a new era in the life of the game.[/p][p]When we first launched Zaccaria Pinball on Steam, it featured only 27 tables and very basic functionality. Back then, we could only hope that over time it would grow into a true pinball universe. Over the years, however, we shaped the game together with the community. Today, there are over 150 tables available, along with countless features that make the game unique in the world of digital pinball.[/p][p]Back then, everything was different. Nine years ago, our goal was to make the game accessible to everyone, so we designed it to run even on 2010-era low/medium laptops. This meant that at the time, we couldn’t fully exploit the graphical capabilities of contemporary hardware.[/p][p]The raytracing implementation in the game doesn’t require GPUs with dedicated raytracing cores. This was important to us because we wanted everyone to enjoy this graphical feature, not just those with the latest and most expensive GPUs. Nine years have passed, and today the minimum supported configuration is an NVIDIA GeForce GT 1030. Thanks to our long-standing development philosophy, even players with a GeForce GT 1030 can enjoy 1080p raytracing options. This GPU is already far more powerful than the originally targeted hardware.[/p][p]Over the years, we’ve added VR support, multiplayer, major graphical upgrades and optimizations, and countless internal settings. All aimed at enhancing the gameplay experience. On multiple occasions, we rewrote the program almost entirely. In our current work, which began earlier this year, we’ve fundamentally redesigned the system again to ensure it remains stable, expandable, and enjoyable for many years to come.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/8ee56a2fb85fb64a6bc31e228277bd62f0c09b95.png"][/img][/p][p]One of the biggest changes is that Zaccaria Pinball now runs on a server-based system, whereas previously it relied solely on Steam. We built this system completely from scratch. It wasn’t easy, but we believe this ensures a long-term, high-quality experience for the community and continuous growth of the game. This decision is also important because our priority has always been that players should not have to buy the content again as a new program. Tables you’ve acquired over the years will remain yours. We believe that community retention, respect for players, and shared experiences are far more important than any short-term revenue.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/2e784e7a3733a20ed3fa66404be3b0f0aee06a0a.png"][/img][/p][p]From the very beginning, we also kept in mind players who don’t want to or for some reason cannot play in online mode. One real-life scenario we considered is this. A user plays on Steam Deck at home in online mode, then takes the game on a trip where no internet is available. That’s why we implemented a system where any earned customizations remain accessible offline. Once the player reconnects to the internet, the game automatically syncs their progress with our servers, ensuring they still receive the XP they earned.[/p][p]Over a month ago, we launched the closed beta. Nearly 50 players enthusiastically supported our work. Countless bug fixes and gameplay improvements were made based on feedback and reports. This month felt long to us because every day brought us closer to sharing the game with a wider audience. It was a challenge to balance fixing bugs and implementing community suggestions, but we chose the latter to ensure a better experience for you.[/p][p]We released the closed beta even though VR and multiplayer weren’t fully re-implemented yet, and the game could mostly only be controlled with a mouse. We sincerely thank the beta testers who spent countless hours testing the server-based system despite these limitations. Along the way, we also added new graphical enhancements. Opal lamps on original Zaccaria tables and 3D prism lamps now feature raytracing for a more lifelike look. Additionally, large pinball table lamps now behave like classic halogen bulbs. They gradually light up and fade, rather than just switching on and off. On older EM tables, Scroll Reels are now correctly simulated.[/p][p]For an authentic experience, we implemented the Carry Over style, but because it can be slow in real life. Especially on retro tables with seven-digit scores. We also added the option to use Direct Drive. The main difference is that Carry Over only drives the first wheel, while the others follow. Whereas in Direct Drive, all wheels spin independently. The new customization menu lets you freely choose which style you prefer.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/65e35e2e159be7639b714d98f8107c1892227f6a.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve completely revamped customization in the game. There’s now a leveling system where you earn XP, unlocking new customization options as you level up. But that’s not all. As shown in earlier screenshots, there’s also a “Magic Market” menu. You might wonder if this requires real money. We managed to avoid microtransactions entirely! The solution is the Tournament system, which includes both official tournaments and player-organized events. Players who place well earn in-game currency, which can be spent in the Magic Market. Additionally, players who purchased the Bronze Pack receive extra customization options.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/a6e2d27737135fed731ec01a8786795d5076e91d.png"][/img][/p][p]The new server-based system allowed us to completely redesign the Achievement system. From now on, in-game Achievements are called [b]Table Tasks[/b], with some still linked to their corresponding Steam Achievements. These Table Tasks are now also saved on our servers.[/p][p]VR controls have been fully re-implemented, like all other features. You can now choose which eye is displayed on the player’s screen, and we’ve redesigned laser pointer handling, making aiming much more precise and easier for UI navigation. Additionally, [b]FFR (Fixed Foveated Rendering)[/b] has been implemented. This keeps the center of your view sharp while gradually reducing detail toward the edges, improving VR performance with minimal impact on clarity. It requires an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.[/p][p]We’ve updated [b]Steam Input[/b] with new actions, which may require you to manually reselect your Steam Input settings. At the same time, we’ve kept the legacy XInput support. XInput button mappings can be adjusted in-game, while Steam Input customization is done through the Steam interface. It’s important to select the correct input method, as the two cannot be used simultaneously.[/p][p]We also implemented the [b]RCAS pass[/b] from FSR 1.0, often used by VR players for extra image sharpness. However, it’s available to all users with a stronger GPU and can be very useful.[/p][p]Another new feature enabled by the server-based system is [b]Quests[/b]. There are daily, weekly, and monthly Quests. Completing them grants XP, helping you level up.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/8ab2b2d126958e33a3f176459b26ff64c0643d2e.png"][/img][/p][p]We’d like to introduce the [b]Tournament system[/b] to help you understand why it was implemented this way. We aimed to recreate the atmosphere of real tournaments. Once a Tournament match starts, there are no breaks. You must complete it in one go. Every pinball hit matters, as official tournaments give a limited number of attempts. This ensures that every shot counts. Official Tournaments come in three types: daily, weekly, and monthly. Players who own the table get more attempts (3/4/5), while those who don’t still get 1/1/2 attempts. Owners can also practice in unlimited Practice mode before the match, following the same rules but without recording scores.[/p][p]There’s also the [b]Custom Tournament[/b], which players can start for 100 Magic Coins. Up to nine Custom Tournaments can run simultaneously, and each player can host only one at a time. Settings are fully customizable: Arcade/Simulation/User(host physical parameters) mode, 3 or 5 balls, and number of attempts. Duration is limited to 24 hours. Winners of both Official and Custom Tournaments earn Magic Coins. If a Custom Tournament is successful, the host is refunded 100 Magic Coins. For detailed rules, please check the in-game description.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/3a53f859394df6202ceb35d2bf0dab445a6f3eb4.png"][/img][/p][p]Recently, beta testers asked how we could better reward players who purchased content. The solution is [b]profile customization[/b]. All players can earn XP and spend Magic Coins in the Magic Market, but the profile banner stripe is reserved for those who have purchased content. This way, everyone receives rewards, while supporting players are specially recognized.[/p][p]Originally, completed Tournaments couldn’t be reviewed, as we were focused on making the system work correctly. Following beta feedback, we added this feature. At the last moment, we also re-implemented [b]replay functionality[/b]. You can now watch matches of the top 3 players during the Tournament, and replays remain available for 30 days after completion.[/p][p]Over the past year, we modified more than [b]40,000 lines of code[/b] in our massive 340,000-line engine/game codebase. Server-side code adds another 32,000+ lines. This doesn’t include third-party libraries.[/p][p]We’re proud that, as a small but passionate and dedicated team, we could work on this project. We know many of you have been with us since the beginning, while others joined later. We sincerely thank all of you for your support, ideas, bug reports, and even criticism. Every piece of feedback helped us make the game better. There were tough times and forced breaks over these nine years, but we never gave up because we always felt it was worth continuing.[/p][p]The version being released now is not the conclusion. It’s a [b]new beginning[/b]. In the coming days, we’ll work on leaving Early Access. For us, leaving Early Access is just a milestone. We will continue developing Zaccaria with the same enthusiasm. We know this version isn’t perfect and never will be, but we strive to release the best version possible. We apologize in advance for any critical bugs you may encounter and will work to fix as many issues as possible.[/p][p]After leaving Early Access, our next milestone is to have [b]Zaccaria Pinball run as a unified version on all platforms[/b] (Nintendo, Android, iOS, PlayStation, Xbox), including shared Tournaments and Leaderboards. We hope this will finally create a true pinball universe where players can compete from anywhere.[/p][p]We know that for veteran players, the new menu structure may feel a bit unfamiliar at first, as we completely redesigned it. Our goal was to create a logical layout that works seamlessly with every input method. We considered touch screens, keyboards, mice, controllers, and VR controls. Creating a menu that met all these criteria wasn’t easy, so in some areas, compromises were necessary. Please share your feedback to let us know if we succeeded. No matter how you play, the experience should remain enjoyable.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/6573249af1dad8d0ffb29ce62d8b60781992f709.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/300c8bb150d3f1614e81bf012eaf6abd9ea53369.png"][/img][/p][p]From the very beginning, it has been our dream to make the game accessible to players who don’t speak English. With more customization options than ever before, supporting multiple languages became a crucial consideration during the rewrite. Accordingly, we designed the UI from the ground up to handle different languages. We’ve successfully translated the game into [b]Hungarian, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Russian, and Dutch[/b]. Special thanks go to the native-speaking beta testers who helped correct language errors. We know some inaccuracies may remain, so we ask native-speaking players to report any issues via bug tickets, and we will fix them. Please note that table rules and in-game DMD/LCD text are not included in the translations.[/p][p]We felt that the original [b]Artwork Table[/b] no longer met modern expectations, so we completely overhauled the Artwork DLC. The Artwork Table is replaced by the [b]Viking Table[/b], featuring deluxe-level table mechanics and a special ability. Before you start playing, you can customize its visuals.[/p][p]This table includes [b]16 individually customizable elements[/b], such as the cabinet interior walls, ramp plastics, pop bumper caps, targets, background, and main playfield components. For each element, you can choose from [b]five different graphic styles[/b], allowing for a unique visual experience every time you play. If you don’t want to spend too much time customizing, there’s also an option to generate a random setup.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/8b9d03916a7581215fba2f697d09b9bdca5c1b2d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This year, every update has included a new table, and this update is no exception.[/p][p]Step up and feel the heat. [b]Star’s Phoenix Deluxe[/b] takes the legendary 1987 classic and turns it into a high-roller’s dream. Dazzling visuals, fast-paced action, and nonstop rewards bring the thrill of the casino floor straight to your screen.[/p][p]Spin the reels of chance with [b]ball save, kickback, multipliers, and sizzling combo shots[/b], then stack up the wins with [b]skillshots, hand bonuses, jackpots, and exclusive access to the VIP poker room and cocktail bar[/b].[/p][p]Choose your game of chance across [b]five unique modes (Poker, Craps, Blackjack, Baccarat, and Roulette[/b]) each packed with its own casino-inspired challenges and risks worth taking. And when the stakes skyrocket, unleash [b]multiball madness[/b] and chase layered objectives that keep the adrenaline flowing.[/p][p]With every flip, [b]Star’s Phoenix Deluxe[/b] captures the glamour, glitz, and energy of a luxury casino. Reimagined for the digital pinball age. Place your bets, hit the lights, and let the good times roll.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/0b2355d063cb010b1fb4d2d83b4b0ded5f5d3613.gif"][/img][/p][p]And that’s not all. We’re also preparing a special surprise, which we’re keeping under wraps for now. But one thing’s for sure. Pinball fans will want to keep an eye out![/p][p]We are deeply grateful for your support throughout this long journey. Without you, this game could never have become what it is today. A constantly expanding pinball experience with over [b]150 tables[/b], offering challenges for every type of player.[/p][p]Now it’s time to celebrate together. [b]Zaccaria Pinball has finally reached its best form yet[/b].[/p][p]For those who love a great soundtrack, the awesome music tracks from this new table are available separately if you own the [b]Zaccaria Pinball - Original Soundtrack DLC[/b]. [/p][p][b]We hope everyone enjoys the new version, and we thank you for continuing to be part of our journey![/b][/p][p][/p][p][i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/4022120/Zaccaria_Pinball__Stars_Phoenix_Deluxe_Pinball_Table/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/859500/Zaccaria_Pinball__Artwork_Editor/"][/dynamiclink] [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/999070/Zaccaria_Pinball__Original_Soundtrack/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Update #105: Time Machine Deluxe, LCD upgrades & exciting news hit this update!
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey Pinball Fans! [/b][/p][p][/p][p]Happy Thursday's update! Today we bring you another [b]Deluxe table[/b], [b]LCD updates[/b] for more Deluxe tables, and some [b]exciting news about the new iteration[/b]. Let’s dive into the details.[/p][p]Our mission to add improved LCD animations to all Deluxe tables has officially reached its conclusion. From now on, [b]every Deluxe table includes the upgraded LCD display[/b] with enhanced visuals and animations.[/p][p]Today’s update adds the new LCD animations to the following tables:[/p][list][*][p]Robot Deluxe[/p][/*][*][p]Combat Deluxe[/p][/*][*][p]Farfalla Deluxe[/p][/*][*][p]Space Shuttle Deluxe[/p][/*][*][p]Zankor Deluxe[/p][/*][/list][p]We hope you enjoy the new look and feel across the entire Deluxe lineup![/p][p]We’re also excited to share that the [b]new system[/b] has reached the stage where we can launch a [b]closed beta test[/b]. This new interface includes groundbreaking features and a fresh user experience that we can't wait for you to explore.[/p][p]Interested in joining the beta? You can apply now on Discord.[/p][p]Please note: [b]This is the final update for the “old” iteration. [/b]All future updates will support the new system only.[/p][p]Now let's talk about the new table.[/p][p]...Wait, is this now? Or then? Or perhaps still to come?[/p][p]Somewhere between last week’s echoes and tomorrow’s code, a new [b]Deluxe Table[/b] materialized.[/p][p]Originally from 1983… or was it 2025? It’s hard to tell when the flippers spin across centuries. The Time Machine is now reborn as the [b]Time Machine Deluxe[/b] table. This table launches you into the [b]past, present, and future[/b], with [b]ball saves[/b], [b]kickbacks[/b], [b]multipliers[/b], [b]combos[/b], and curious powers like [b]Future Boost[/b] and [b]Time Warp[/b].[/p][p]Complete eight main missions, (each representing a letter of “[b]TIMELINE[/b]”) and chase strange phenomena like [b]Paradox[/b], [b]Continuum[/b], [b]Chronology[/b], and [b]Wormhole[/b]. Every shot brings a twist in time.[/p][p]Become the master of timeline now.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/9981e7f9d4067e02a5180bac8d33982adc65f694.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]For those who love a great soundtrack, the awesome music tracks from this new table are available separately if you own the [b]Zaccaria Pinball - Original Soundtrack DLC[/b]. [/p][p]As always we appreciate your unbroken support towards our work![/p][p][/p][p][i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3776470/Zaccaria_Pinball__Time_Machine_Deluxe_Pinball_Table/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/999070/Zaccaria_Pinball__Original_Soundtrack/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Update #104: Granada Deluxe lands with fresh LCD upgrades and Early Access news
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey Pinball Fans! [/b][/p][p][/p][p]Welcome to [b]another Thursday update[/b]! Today, we bring you a [b]brand-new Deluxe table[/b]. Following our [b]recent fiesta in Mexico[/b], we’re now [b]sailing [/b]across the [b]Atlantic[/b] straight [b]into [/b]the [b]heart of Andalusia[/b].[/p][p]We’re continuing our mission to upgrade [b]LCD animations[/b] for earlier Deluxe tables. This time, four more have received the treatment: [b]Strike Deluxe[/b], [b]Universe Deluxe[/b], [b]Pool Champion Deluxe[/b], and [b]House of Diamonds Deluxe[/b]. These visual LCD upgrades aim to enhance your gameplay experience and keep the Deluxe lineup feeling fresh and unified.[/p][p]But before we talk more about the new table, we want to update you. We’re [b]still working hard[/b] on the [b]new iteration of Zaccaria Pinball[/b]. [b]Internal testing[/b] went [b]well[/b], but there are still a [b]few missing features[/b] and [b]some stubborn bugs [/b]we need to [b]finish baking[/b] before we can [b]share it with you[/b]. We’re [b]already[/b] on the [b]home stretch[/b]! Please note that, once we [b]exit Early Access[/b], [b]prices will increase[/b]. The game will remain [b]free to play[/b], but this DLC [b]price adjustment[/b] is necessary to support future growth.[/p][p]Now, onto the table.[/p][p][b]Granada Deluxe[/b] invites you to the [b]heart of southern Spain[/b], where vibrant rhythms echo through cobbled streets, and ancient architecture tells tales of a rich and layered history. Just like the city itself, the table is a feast of color, energy, and surprises from the ornate towers of the Cathedral multipliers, to the sizzling tension of the Paella Bonus.[/p][p]You’ll roam [b]local markets[/b],[b] battle bulls[/b] in [b]thrilling pop bumper[/b] challenges, and [b]spin[/b] your way through [b]bubbling fountains[/b] as you [b]chase jackpots[/b] and mini games across two dynamic upper playfields. Whether you’re lighting the [b]WAY[/b], unlocking the [b]CITADEL[/b], or gathering ingredients in culinary-themed game modes like [b]Soup[/b], [b]Spices[/b], and [b]Spicy Cake[/b], [b]Granada Deluxe[/b] is packed with personality and scoring potential.[/p][p]Let the music guide you, light the [b]T-E-A[/b] and [b]S-P-A[/b] lamps for [b]ball saves[/b], and don’t forget to stir the pot, because this table rewards strategy, timing, and flair.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/c96484f0dbc2838b9cfd93c1da4fd79fa0ec691d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]For those who love a great soundtrack, the awesome music tracks from this new table are available separately if you own the [b]Zaccaria Pinball - Original Soundtrack DLC[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p]A big thank you, as always, for your continued support and feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]And one more thing. Want to see [b]Granada Deluxe[/b] in action? [/p][p][b]Duveline[/b] will be live-streaming the table today on [b]Twitch at 9 PM CEST[/b].[/p][p]Watch it here: [dynamiclink href="https://twitch.tv/duveline"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p][p][i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b][/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3776460/Zaccaria_Pinball__Granada_Deluxe_Pinball_Table/"][/dynamiclink] [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/999070/Zaccaria_Pinball__Original_Soundtrack/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Update #103: Mexico Deluxe debuts with vibrant play and LCD animation upgrades
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey Pinball Fans! [/b][/p][p][/p][p]It’s [b]Thursday[/b] again! Right [b]before the Steam Summer Sale[/b], we dropped an [b]update[/b] to keep things moving. Now that the [b]sale is almost over[/b], we’re back with [b]another one [/b]to spark your flippers with [b]fresh energy[/b]! notes.title: Update #100 – Magic Castle Deluxe & Beyond
notes.content:
[b]Hey Pinball Fans![/b]

Happy Thursday! We’re back with a fresh update to keep your flippers warm and your scores climbing!

Over the past few months our team has been split into three groups (table design, new Zaccaria features / bug fixing and a secret project). Now, that secret project and the main Zaccaria development have been merged, so you won’t see any extra surprises in this update, but rest assured our table-making crew is still working at full tilt!

The latest addition to our Deluxe series is Magic Castle Deluxe table, which invites you to a legendary pinball quest set in a mystical, alternate-medieval kingdom. Uncover hidden dungeons beneath the castle, and face off against mythical beasts and dragons. Master the enchanted ramps, trigger modes, and harness multiballs as you ascend through the castle’s secrets. Are you ready to wield the flippers of fate and become the ultimate Pinball Wizard?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/1f66a0fae7467ca371028b3d30cf5772666781f5.gif[/img]

For those who love a great soundtrack, the awesome music tracks from this new table are available separately if you own the [b]Zaccaria Pinball - Original Soundtrack DLC[/b].

And now, here comes the surprise. This is our 100th Steam update. Originally, we’d planned to mark this milestone with a brand-new beginning, as we hinted back in January. Earlier this year, we made a bold decision and completely rewrote the bulk of the Zaccaria codebase to lay down a modern, scalable, rock-solid foundation. This under-the-hood overhaul means we will be able to develop more efficiently going forward.

This will also mark the 5th major iteration of Zaccaria Pinball in its twelve-year lifespan. [b]Sadly, we are not quite ready to publish this new iteration yet, but we see the light at the end of the tunnel.[/b]

The initial version launched on iOS on March 27, 2013, with just three tables: Time Machine, Locomotion, and Devil Riders.

We want to thank everyone who has been with us since the beginning.

Our Steam release went live on June 16, 2016, with 38 tables. This milestone would not have been possible without you, since we first had to get through Steam Greenlight (we submitted on Jan 21, 2016). After six months on Greenlight, we launched in Early Access, which gave us the opportunity to refine the game and add even more content for pinball fans.

Hard to believe, but the first version of Zaccaria Pinball didn’t include any achievements. On Jul 15, 2016 It was our 3rd update that introduced achievements for just three tables: Time Machine, Locomotion, and Devil Riders. Today, we have around 5,000 Steam achievements. Just four months later, on October 17, 2016, VR support was introduced. Then, one month after that, on November 18, 2016, we released our 30th update, which marked the beginning of new table content additions. We implemented real-time ray-traced shadows on December 16, 2016, with our 33rd update as an 'early Christmas present.' The feature even worked in the VR version. This was almost two years ahead of the RTX era and well before ray tracing became a defining feature in modern gaming.

Each update includes numerous bug fixes. The list goes on and on. If you'd like more details, please check the News section.

Now, after the 100th update, Zaccaria Pinball boasts 160 tables. That means 122 brand-new creations added over nearly nine years of development. Breaking it down, we’ve released at least one fresh table every month on average, even though we had a few years development gap.

This new iteration retains our entirely custom-developed game and physics engine, along with the familiar Zaccaria gameplay, making it feel like you’ve stepped into “Zaccaria Pinball 2”. Importantly, the new in-game coins can only be earned through play and cannot be purchased with real money. Plus, every achievement you have earned, every high score you have posted, and every DLC you have bought stays safe and sound!

Without saying any more, we're leaking a picture of the new look that speaks for itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/b509cf3d8d642b6544b9a05a61c7b96f6cc2c2ec.jpg[/img]
[b]This is a development preview of a possible future look.[/b]

After we release this 5th iteration, Zaccaria Pinball will step out of Early Access and become a full, finished game.

This milestone means we’ve crafted a version of Zaccaria Pinball that reaches the same level of completeness as the classic games of the ’90s. Back then there were no patches and what shipped was truly the final product. It was not only a golden era for video games but also for pinball itself. A time when machines stood proudly in arcades and perfection was built right into the glass and steel. We respect that legacy and we’re proud to deliver a game we can finally call “done”. That is the very reason we have spent so long in Early Access. “Done” doesn’t mean the end of content. It marks the beginning of a new phase, built on solid ground, much like the expansion packs of the past.

We’ll be leaving behind an important milestone, but that does not mean we’re done developing.

We’re continuously working to eliminate bugs and improve your gameplay experience. Check out our dedicated Bug Reports discussion for detailed info on the fixes.

Thank you for your continued support and feedback. See you in the next update!

[i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b]

notes.title: Update #98: Early Release - Soccer King Deluxe, Battle Tank and Bug Fixes
notes.content:
[b]Hey Pinball Fans![/b]

We’re back with another exciting update a little earlier than usual!
Due to a national holiday in Hungary, this week’s update drops one day ahead of schedule. We didn’t want you to wait any longer than necessary for the latest features and fixes!

Let’s kick things off with the technical improvements.

We’ve tackled a few important issues reported by the community:
[list]
[*] [b]OpenGL version fallback function fix.[/b] After introducing FSR, we updated the OpenGL version from 3.3 to 4.5. Unfortunately, the fallback mechanism didn’t work as expected, leading to crashes for some players using older hardware.
[*] [b]Improved Display Mode setting.[/b] In some scenarios, the Display Mode setting wasn’t functioning correctly, which could lead to display and performance issues. We've reworked the behavior for greater consistency and fewer surprises.
[*] [b]The drivers will now prioritize stronger GPUs by default for Zaccaria.[/b] This resolves the issue where the game could automatically run on a weaker (integrated or energy-saving) graphics card, particularly affecting laptop users.
[*] [b]Improved screen handling for cabinet users.[/b] It is now possible to assign the 4th display as a playfield, dmd, or backglass screen within the existing cabinet setup options. 
[*] [b]Award Table Improvements.[/b] Starting from the City Golf Award table, we’ve begun systematically fixing bugs and polishing the Award series tables. These updates address long-standing issues and improve gameplay quality across the board. Expect more consistency and a better overall experience as we refined these special tables.
[*] [b]Memory leak mitigation.[/b] We've significantly reduced the occurrence of a previously reported memory leak. While not fully eliminated yet, the issue no longer leads to crashes or instability during typical use. In internal testing, even after 80 table launches, no critical problems were observed.
[/list]
While we’ve resolved many bugs in this update, a few known issues remain that we’re actively working on. These only occur when using [b]Borderless Display Mode[/b]:
[list]
[*] [b]on PC[/b] – When AMD Virtual Super Resolution (VSR) is enabled, activating a backglass or DMD screen in Cabinet Mode can cause the playfield resolution to exceed the screen’s boundaries.
[*] [b]on Mac[/b] – In Cabinet Mode, the playfield screen cannot currently be reassigned while using Borderless Display Mode.
[*] [b]on Linux[/b] – Borderless Mode may not initialize correctly until ALT+TAB is pressed twice. This temporarily resolves the issue.

notes.title: Update #97: Hop Into Three New Tables, Hunted Multiple Bugs And More.
notes.content:
[b]Hey Pinball Fans![/b]

Our next update is here, just in time for Easter! To celebrate the season of surprises, we’re releasing three new tables: one Deluxe and two Award series additions (including a long-lost gem from 2011). Plus, we're unveiling something special outside the game too…
As always, we appreciate your bug reports and testing. Your feedback helps make the game better for everyone! This update focuses heavily on improving performance and fixing issues. 

Here are some major fixes:
[list]
[*] [b]Multi-Screen Crash Fix (PC & macOS).[/b] For more details, check out our previous devlog.
[*] [b]Resolved memory leak[/b] from Steam overlay. 
[*] [b]Improved macOS external display support. [/b]
[*] [b]Improved macOS window mode support.[/b] Now the Full Screen mode is the Exclusive Full-Screen Mode and the Borderless is the native (green button) full-screen mode. 
[*] [b]Fixed In-game UI visibility[/b] settings, now the NONE option behaves as expected.
[*] [b]Improved the in-game DMD[/b] panel and now hidden in VR.
[*] [b]Fixed borderless mode[/b] flickering issue.
[*] [b]Renamed windows[/b] for easier use for streamers. Now it's easier to find the game windows with your favourite capture application.
[/list]
Some known issue:
[list]
[*] On Linux, in Borderless mode, you have to press ALT + TAB twice to work correctly.
[*] There is a not yet found memory leak in our engine. It is possible that the game crashes after 20-30 table changes.
[/list]
For a full breakdown of all known issues and updates, visit the Bug Reports section in the community forums.

Now, let’s talk about the exciting [b]new tables[/b]!

The first table is the [b]Moon Flight Deluxe[/b] table which joins our Deluxe series. Based on Zaccaria's 1976 electro-mechanical table Moon Flight, this reimagined Deluxe version takes the spirit of the original and launches it into the cosmos with a modern twist. Get ready for a dazzling journey through space, complete with vibrant visuals and a fully remastered soundtrack. Whether you're a nostalgic fan of the original Moon Flight or discovering this celestial classic for the first time, Moon Flight Deluxe is a pinball mission you don’t want to abort.

Prepare for launch… and don’t forget to check the engine before you leave orbit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/d9022793f93d469c5a1e3bc9e979fb1dcb6f1750.gif[/img]

Next on the crime list straight from the vault is the Gangsters table, which is an unreleased original table we began developing way back in 2011. For years, it sat forgotten on the shelf, but now we’ve dusted it off, retooled the rules, and brought it back to life.

Step into the shadowy world of 90s underworld legends, where loyalty is currency and power can only be earned in one way. In [b]Gangsters[/b], you'll place your bets, crack the safe, arm yourself and climb the criminal ranks with scores. How to get this table? notes.title: Devlog Update: Tackling Multi-Screen and macOS Issues
notes.content:
[b]Hey Pinball Fans![/b]

We value your support and feedback, and we want you to know that we’re actively ironing out issues to deliver the best possible pinball experience.

[b]We’ve fixed a crash issue that was affecting some players using multiple screens. After a lot of investigation, we discovered that the problem was related to how the Steam overlay interacts with the game. It wasn’t easy to track down, but the issue has now been resolved. We also addressed a similar problem on macOS. The fix will be included in Thursday’s update.[/b]

[b]Thank you for your patience and support as we continue improving the game![/b]

If you're curious about what caused these issues and how we fixed them, we’d love to share a bit more detail. It turned out to be a deceptively simple problem with a not-so-simple solution, and we had to get a little creative to work around it. Here's what happened behind the scenes:

Some of you have reported crashes on setups with a second or third screen. After a thorough investigation, we discovered that the underlying problem was very simple. In addition to this, we want to be transparent about our development process. We do not use the Steam version of our build during development, which meant that we didn’t catch this issue early on. It was only once players experienced the game on Steam that we were able to identify and address the problem.

Steam overlays its interface without distinguishing between the main game window and additional ones. This means that every time our game refreshed the content on any window, the overlay reinitialized itself. This constant reinitialization was causing a memory leak in the Steam overlay’s implementation.

However, the solution to this issue was far from straightforward. With no available API from Steam to restrict or manage the overlay’s behavior, our team had to think outside the box. Instead of refreshing the content on the second and third windows, we reverted to a legacy OpenGL function that updates the content without triggering a full screen refresh. In doing so, we moved away from using double buffering for these additional windows. Instead, we adopted a single buffer setup. By avoiding the full screen refresh altogether, we stopped the overlay from repeatedly reinitializing and switching windows, effectively preventing the memory leak.

We also identified an issue affecting our macOS users. Our Metal implementation was not handling external displays correctly. Since we develop on a MacBook Air (M1, 2020) without an external display, we had only been verifying the built-in screen. 

Meanwhile, we saw a memory leak problem in our macOS implementation.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25288195/97e858d8cd95b61f8d775a3f95e8617cf16e7023.png[/img]
This fix was not easy, as it involved debugging across multiple programming languages (C++ and Objective-C). Once we identified the root cause, we were able to address the issue successfully.

[i]Happy flipping,[/i]
[b]The Magic Pixel Team[/b]

notes.title: Achievement Overhaul: Staying Under Steam's 5000 Limit
notes.content:
Hey Pinball Fans!

When we started implementing achievements in Zaccaria Pinball around 2016, we designed our achievement system so that every table would receive nearly the same number of achievements. We were committed to ensuring that achievements were enjoyable for everyone. Therefore, we created a varied mix of light and challenging experiences roughly corresponding to 25–50 achievement types. In 2016, the number of achievements grew extremely rapidly, and for a short while, we led Steam in achievement counts.

Unfortunately, games soon appeared where you could earn 100–200 achievements with just a click for a single event.

Around 2017, Steam decided that the maximum number of achievements in a game could only be 5000. We discussed with Steam that in our game, achievements aren’t merely empty, filler numbers that are artificially inflated, and we inquired whether it would be possible to have more than 5000 achievements. Unfortunately, our request was rejected.

Around 2020, when we reached the 5000 limit and could no longer create new achievements. We made the decision to modify our tables so that we would consistently remain within the 5000 limit. As Steam does not offer any other way to continue supporting this feature on our newly released tables. We decided to make wiser use of our remaining achievement quota. As a result, we are omitting the easier achievements.

Thus, our tables will include approximately 10–15 achievements.

Happy flipping,
The Magic Pixel Team

We’ve been hard at work behind the scenes, and now it’s time to show you everything we’ve been working on.

First up, we’re thrilled to introduce the Blackbelt Deluxe table! This brand-new addition is packed with action and designed to keep you flipping for hours of fun.

And there’s more. We’ve gone the extra mile and completely overhauled the 27 existing retro tables. Instead of reusing the original art, we’ve created brand-new graphics that give these timeless classics a fresh, vibrant style. It’s the same retro gameplay you love, but now with a modern and polished look.

Still with us? Great, because here’s another big update. We’ve also revamped the 13 existing Deluxe tables with brand-new visuals. These updates bring a consistent and refined style to the Deluxe collection, making them even more immersive and exciting to play.

[b]And now for the best news of all![/b]

We’ve also updated the Remake tables, giving them the same treatment as the Deluxe tables. The remakes now feature a modern, consistent art style that no longer uses the original artwork from their Solid-State and Electro-Mechanical counterparts. The only things they share with the originals are their themes and names. Everything else has been completely reimagined. This is a massive transformation, and we can’t wait for you to experience it.

We almost forgot to mention. We’ve replaced the music in both Red Show Deluxe and Spooky Deluxe! The new tracks are from the same composer who created the music for the Blackbelt Deluxe table. Get ready for a fresh, exciting soundtrack that will elevate your gameplay experience even more!

We encourage you to revisit every Remake, Retro, and Deluxe table. The changes are huge, and we’re confident you’ll love the fresh new look!

We hope you’re as excited as we are to jump back into Zaccaria Pinball with all these incredible updates. Thank you for being such an amazing community. Your support means so much to us. Now, grab those flippers, rack up some high scores, and let us know what you think.

Finally, stay tuned. We have big plans for this year and can’t wait to share them with you! We are committed to working with the same energy and dedication as we did in the past. Our goal is to bring back the excitement of regular updates, just like the good old days.

[b]And one last thing…[/b]

We’ve rewritten our engine to support the Metal API under macOS, along with native ARM support. 

For our Linux fans, we’ve fixed the AMD graphics issue, which also resolves the Steam Deck problem. Make sure to run Zaccaria Pinball with Steam Linux Native 1.0 (scout) to access the native implementation. Without this, Zaccaria Pinball will not run.

Additionally, we’ve fixed the VR implementation. It now works seamlessly with the Oculus Quest 3 via Steam Link. A small note: if you modify the eye resolution in the Steam interface, you will need to restart Zaccaria Pinball for the changes to take effect.

notes.title: Update #75
notes.content:
Come On Hit The Special!

This update is special indeed! The new Star God remake table has arrived! The remake tables started in 2016 and were our first attempt at introducing new content to the game with features found on modern pinball tables. Now that 27 "Remake" tables have been made we are moving on to the next table category called "Deluxe".

What exactly the Deluxe tables will entail is not yet known, however, we will make sure to follow up in the future explaining more about these new tables.

[h1][b]NEW DLC: STAR GOD 2019 TABLE[/b][/h1]
http://store.steampowered.com/app/1159530/

[h1][b]UPDATED DLC: ZACCARIA PINBALL - ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK[/b][/h1]
http://store.steampowered.com/app/999070/

notes.title: What is next?
notes.content:
Hey pinball fans,

Last week, we released update #74 and introduced the new Time Machine remake table. While players are playing the new Time Machine table, we are currently working on the next and last remake table.

Even though the last remake is currently being developed, we will still release new updates and deliver interesting content like deluxe tables for example to you in the future.

Earlier this week, we have also re-released Zaccaria Pinball on Android, meaning you can now play Zaccaria Pinball on your mobile phone and everywhere you want on the same graphics experience like Steam version.

You can check our new app in the link below:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hu.magicpixel.Zaccaria&hl=en

Thank you for your support!

[h1][b]NEW MENU DESIGN[/b][/h1]
The game has a new flat menu design to be compatible with portrait and landscape modes. Also because of the new design the touch screen controlling is way better than before. Some of the menu points have been relocated to a more suitable menu, so please do not be surprised if you find a setting in another menu. From now on every setting has a hint text, so you have an idea what you change. The menus are more operable in VR mode thanks to the new design (although VR menus need some more development in the future).

notes.title: Status Update for Linux version
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25288195/98444b875747d8dcb8753703165fdd56a363d5b1.png[/img]

First of all, we would like to apologize for the last update that made Zaccaria Pinball unplayable for some players on Linux.

In the last few weeks, we have worked on solving those issues. As a result of these fixes, we have to modify the minimum requirements for Linux players. Starting from Update #68, Linux players will require at least Ubuntu version 16.04 to play with Zaccaria Pinball.

Because SteamVR got updated in the past we also now have to make changes and update the game.

The current version of SteamVR library requires GCC version 4.9. 

However, Ubuntu 14.04 repository still includes version GCC 4.8. Because the game always loads the VR library GCC 4.9 has to be installed from the source if you want to play on 14.04.

Also, we made a GUI for dependencies so you can see what's missing.

See the sample picture below. From now on zlib and libpng are changed from dynamics linking to static linking for less dependencies errors.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25288195/5255835d929beebc27c063fa33ba493e6136df56.png[/img]

[b]We would like to thank all Linux players for their understanding and patience. Update #68 should be released at end of next week. [/b]

notes.title: Update #64
notes.content:
Our plan was to release 27 retro tables, and in Update 64, we have released the last few retro tables. Since Top Hand table has been released, we are happy to announce that all the tables we planned from the Zaccaria pinball company are now implemented.

We will announce soon what new features and tables we are working on and what to expect in the future. Meanwhile we are also working on the Nintendo Switch version and looking to release the game on new platforms.

We would like to thank for your support by purchasing of Gold or Platinum Pack. As a gratitude 27 free retro tables have been added to these packs. We hope this has been appealed to your enjoy. If you still want to support us please write a review of your opinion. Thank you!

Don’t forget to follow our Facebook page for global news, sweepstakes and other interesting information.
https://www.facebook.com/zaccariapinball/

notes.title: Update #61
notes.content:
Here is a new update with 5 new tables. Also with a surprise that would be a gift for you!

This is not a usual update since huge developments have been happened in the engine.
[b]Because of that performance issue can be happaned.[/b]

ZP used 1 core so far, now it uses multicore that affects on loading, physics, sounds and script handling. This modification brought you faster running and some small improvements. This step had to be done because of console builds, like Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, iOS, Android, to run the same build on all of them and they will have the same updates.

Here are additional features of this update:

1. Artwork Editor
This mode includes a table with 2 differences.

The 1st difference:
The table has similar rules as other Zaccaria table but you collect extra coins that can be spent for customization items. You can edit artworks of the playfield and the covers and you can place together artworks of the table this way by an in-built editor. Here you can use your imagination and do that you have not do anywhere else.

The 2nd difference:
Everybody who purchases this mode will be a participant of a sweepstake where you can win a palpable gift. 5 pieces of handmade Mini Pinball model scaled 1/12 (made from wood, plexi and stainless steel, by sublimation printing, sticker-free) will be raffled in 1 month later.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/859500/

notes.title: Controller problems
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25288195/8cc88577ddc4c2477acd6238d06dc1f6e854d3ac.jpg[/img]

We have noticed that many players are having issues with the new controller handling that came with the last update. We have made some controller related changes on the Steam Partner page that might solve the issue.

Explanation:
If the Xbox 360, Xbox One, PS4 or Generic Controller support is checked in Big Picture mode, this results in input control being lost. The setting of Steam Controller API has to be set to ENABLED to make the controller work.

If Xbox 360, Xbox One, PS4 or Generic Controller support is unchecked in the Big Picture mode, then the setting of Steam Controller API (enabled or disabled) in the game is not relevant and the controller(s) are handled by Xinput instead.

Steam Controller API option works properly when a Steam Controller is used. Enable turns on it, disable turns off it.

If a controller with Steam Controller API is used, then the game disables Xinput because we have found an issue during the development that prevents that execution in some cases. Because of this, pushing of, for example, the button A, is detected twice, that caused double click on a menu setting, for example, because its signal was transmitted through Steam Controller API and Xinput too.

[b]We still like to thank all the players and fans for all the help and support in the Early Access period. We will continue to fix bugs and tackle issues that are currently in the game.
We may not directly address every bug thread, but we are aware of what is happening in the Steam discussion forum.[/b]

If Xbox 360, Xbox One, PS4 or Generic Controller support is unchecked in the Big Picture mode, then the setting of Steam Controller API (enabled or disabled) in the game is not relevant and the controller(s) are handled by Xinput instead.

Steam Controller API option works properly when a Steam Controller is used. Enable turns on it, disable turns off it.

If a controller with Steam Controller API is used, then the game disables Xinput because we have found an issue during the development that prevents that execution in some cases. Because of this, pushing of, for example, the button A, is detected twice, that caused double click on a menu setting, for example, because its signal was transmitted through Steam Controller API and Xinput too.

[b]We still like to thank all the players and fans for all the help and support in the Early Access period. We will continue to fix bugs and tackle issues that are currently in the game.
We may not directly address every bug thread, but we are aware of what is happening in the Steam discussion forum.[/b]

notes.title: Update #46 - Sponsored by Easter Bunny
notes.content:
Easter Bunny has been here and brought 2 Easter eggs. One of them includes a new modern table, Circus 2017. Unfortunately the other egg had a crack so it brings an online multiplayer option with beta version.

[b]Circus 2017[/b]
The speciality of this table brings a new kind of challenge to ZP players. You have 2 balls at every round. Depending on your pinball skills you are able to complete all modes with 2 balls even.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25288195/6d1d90766aac875768b525b2139f72729cfbf652.png[/img]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/623790

[b]Online Multiplayer[/b]
This feature is in very alpha stage, so issues can be happend for sure! This mode supports up to 4 players on Time Machine and all unlocked tables (free mode is not supported on those tables). Players are coming one after another and the order is defined by number of their SteamIDs.

[h1]We wish you a Happy Easter![/h1]

notes.title: Online Multiplayer is coming soon!
notes.content:
Hey pinball fans!

Here is a time to make a new announcement about a newer awesome feature that will be available soon in beta stage. The 'Online Multiplayer' supports up to 4 players one after the other like when you went to an arcade with your friends to play some pinball.

The 'Online Multiplayer' is available for everybody on Time Machine table for free. On other tables you have to have a purchased DLC that disables score limitation to be able to play with.

notes.title: Pinball Editor is coming
notes.content:
We would like to share with you a fantastic news. We have been working on a pinball editor for Zaccaria Pinball for a while. Today an important milestone has been achieved, a prototype table is done. Please check the pre-alpha picture! Yes, this table is designed from about 20 pinball parts by the pinball editor.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25288195/5d6a7e534b0ebc14aa26552b60847511c363a767.png[/img]

One of the most important goals is as easy usage as possible. You are able to select objects, like pop bumpers and their textures from a grid and put them on the playfield simply.

At the moment more than 200 different pinball parts are available to use and this number will be expanded updates by updates. Many pinball parts would be familier from golden era of pinball history. This way you can build similar pinball table of that era.

The pinball editor will be available as a paid DLC.

More information is coming soon.

notes.title: Introduction of TOURNAMENT MODE with unique replay feature
notes.content:
By release of update #43 we introduce a new mode called Tournament that is still in beta phase.

At the moment you are able to play on one table (Shooting the Rapids) with 3 balls and simulation physics (Free Mode is not available). Replay and score of your best result will be uploaded (internet connection is needed, offline mode is not available) and able to download and watch other players by clicking to small replay icon next to his/her name and score on the leaderboards (see attached screenshot).

This is the first step of development for Tournament mode. More features and options will be coming in the future.

Have fun!

notes.title: The Flare Path: Topical Titbits
notes.content: In the alphabetical news round-up waiting like a pre-pounce puma beyond the break ‘A’ is more likely to be for ‘airship’ or ‘angry house’ than ‘apple’. Stripy ungulates probably won’t feature in the entry for ‘Z’ but simulated Bf 110s or Mitsubishi A5Ms might. If you’ve an eye for a shapely engine nacelle or a finely chiselled turret if you’ve an interest in the bloodier bits of history – I guarantee your curiosity will be piqued by something in the 26-compartment specimen drawer below. … [visit site to read more]
